rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable warns those against whom judgment is due and gives glad tidings to those who follow the Reminder; it aptly serves as the heart of Yasin.
rows.anchor: gerek üzerlerine kavil hak olanları inzar ve gerek zikre ittibâ‘edenleri tebşir sadedinde Peygamber’e mev‘ud olan inkılâbâtın mühim bir misâlini vermektedir ki buna bu itibarla “Yâsîn’in kalbi” denilse sezâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Roman pagans' defeat before Christianity prefigures states falling before Islam, when the promise in 9:33 will be manifest.
rows.anchor: Nasrâniyetin karşısında müşrik Romalılar nasıl söndüyse İslâmiyetin karşısında da öyle devletler sukūt edecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is reported to be Antioch and its messengers to have been sent from among Jesus' disciples.
rows.anchor: Burada bu karye Antakya, mürselûn da Îsâ aleyhisselâm’ın Havâriyyûnundan gönderilenler olduğu naklediliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this identification, the people of the town are the inhabitants of the country, the Romans.
rows.anchor: O hâlde “ashâb-ı karye” ashâb-ı memleket ve zikrolunan kavim Romalılar olduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plain sense indicates that the messengers were envoys granted prophethood by God.
rows.anchor: bunların taraf-ı ilâhîden nübüvvet verilmiş resuller olduklarını

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the townspeople's address, 'you are only humans like us,' as evidence that the messengers were prophets, since such a dispute is with prophets.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: “أَنتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve Ka‘b
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b also hold that the messengers were prophets.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’ın ve Ka‘b’ın kavli de budur

rows.speaker: Katâde ve gayrıları
rows.claim: Qatada and others say these were apostles from Jesus' disciples, sent when Jesus was raised up.
rows.anchor: Katâde ve gayrıları demişlerdir ki bunlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Jesus sent the disciples, the verse says 'We sent' because Jesus' mission was itself by God's command.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Îsâ tarafından gönderilmeleri de Allah teâlâ’nın emriyle olduğundan dolayı olmuş oluyor

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify the first two as John and Paul and the third as Simon Peter.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu ikisinın Yuhanna ile Pavlus olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since representation is the passage's chief aim, the strengthening of two by a third signals the honor of Muhammad's apostleship: Muhammad's message confirms and strengthens the missions of Moses and Jesus.
rows.anchor: Yani ikinin bir üçüncü ile takviyesi Mûsâ ve Îsâ aleyhimesselâm’ın ahîren risâlet-i Muhammediye ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople deny revelation, apostleship, scripture, and human prophethood; although pagan idolaters, the Romans did not deny God's existence.
rows.anchor: Romalılar müşrik putperest idiler, bununla beraber Allah’ı inkâr etmemişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from the city's far end is the courageous preacher and martyr known as Habib al-Najjar, the Companion of Yasin, honored by God.
rows.anchor: bu sevgili şehid, Sâhib-i Yâsîn “Habîb-i Neccar” diye mâruftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medine means city and its farthest part means the remote end; this implies the messengers' preaching and the townspeople's treatment of them were heard throughout the city, so clear communication had occurred.
rows.anchor: “Medine” şehir demektir. “Medinenin aksâsı” şehrin en ucu, ta öte başı demek oluyor ki resullerin teblîgātı ve onlara karşı edilen muâmele şehrin her tarafından işitilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is said to be Antioch, then a large and extensive city.
rows.anchor: Bu medine de Antakya’dır diyorlar ve o zaman büyük ve geniş bir şehir olduğunu söylüyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may also mean one of the country's most prominent men, rather than a man literally from its distant edge.
rows.anchor: “medinenin aksâsından” demek, o memleket ricâlinin en ileri gelenlerinden bir zat mânasını da andırır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing that the messengers were in danger, the man came running and exerted himself to guide people and model faithful conduct.
rows.anchor: koşuyordu yani koşarak geldi, ehl-i imana numûne olmak, irşad etmek için bütün cehdiyle çalışıyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He opens with the compassion of shared townspeople, then declares his faith and identifies the messengers as God's envoys.
rows.anchor: evvelâ hemşehrilik şefkatini ileri sürerek nasihati takdim ve onların resul olduklarını ihbar ile imanını izhar eyledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers seek no payment or worldly advantage, removing one reason a traveler might reject a guide.
rows.anchor: sizden bir ecir istemez dünyevî bir garaz u ivaz talep etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His divided argument is that a traveler might reject a guide for an exorbitant fee or lack of trustworthiness, but neither obstacle applies; even if the men were not apostles, their guidance and sincerity leave no reason to refuse them.
rows.anchor: Bunlar ise hem bir ücret istemiyorlar, hem hidâyet sâhibi zatlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'why should I not worship my Creator?' supplies the decisive reason to worship and gently admonishes the audience through compassionate indirection.
rows.anchor: söz irşadda telattuf için ibrâz-ı şefkatle beliğ bir ta‘rîzdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His personal duty to worship his Creator is self-evident; by analogy he asks why his listeners would not worship the Lord who created them, without excuse or impediment.
rows.anchor: Ben sizi kendim gibi düşünüyorum, ben beni yaratana kulluk etmeyi borcum, vazifem bilirim, çünkü beni yaratmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since everyone will be returned to God, avoiding His worship makes no sense.
rows.anchor: hep döndürülüp O’na götürüleceksiniz o hâlde O’na kulluktan nasıl kaçınırsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Merciful wills harm for him, the intercession of other gods will do nothing and they cannot rescue him, so none can be divine.
rows.anchor: O’ndan başka tapılanların benden yana şefaatleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking gods besides the Merciful Creator would put him in manifest error.
rows.anchor: apaçık bir dalâl içindeyimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading addresses the messengers: under attack, the man confesses his faith and asks them to witness it for testimony before God in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ, mürselîne hitabdır; halkın öldürmek için hücûmu üzerine onlara şöyle ikrar verip işhad etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading addresses his people: he believes in the Lord who created them and urges them to listen and follow the messengers.
rows.anchor: İkincisi, yine kavmine hitabdır ki şöyle demek olur: Haberiniz olsun ben O sizi yaratan Rabbinize şüphesiz iman ettim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility addresses all future people capable of hearing, or makes the statement an oath asking them to heed his story and virtues.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü, istikbâlin insanları da dâhil olmak üzere duymak kābiliyeti olan umûma hitab veya kasem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being told to enter the Garden means he was martyred and honored with immediate entry; martyrs in God's path all meet this end.
rows.anchor: yani şehid edildi, doğrudan doğru cennete girmekle ikram olundu, ki Allah yolunda şehid olanlar hep böyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even after his people killed him, he bears no grudge and wishes they would know God's forgiveness and honor, repent of their disbelief, and turn to faith, obedience, and sacrifice for God's cause.
rows.anchor: kavmi hakkında böyle temennide bulundu, demek kavmini unutuvermemiş, gayz u intikam da beslememiş, düşmanlarına bile merhamet eden evliyâ rûhuyla istemişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wish that his people know his blessed fate also carries a measure of self-congratulation or boasting.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber bu temenni, bir mübâhat mânasından hâlî de değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account prompts the question of what God did to the people who killed this heroic preacher and fighter, leading into the following passage.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir suâle karşı buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought a decayed bone to the Prophet, crumbled it, and asked about its revival; the Prophet replied that God would resurrect him too and cast him into the Fire, and this verse was revealed on that occasion.
rows.anchor: Übey b. Halef Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’in huzûruna bir çürümüş kemikle gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every creature's details, including all its gathered and scattered parts, roots, branches, conditions, qualities, quantities, and particular features.
rows.anchor: her mahlûku bütün tafsîlâtıyla, her birinin toplanan ve dağılan bütün eczâsı, usûl ü fürû‘u, evzâ‘ı, ahvâli, keyfiyyât ve kemmiyyâtı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He knows every mode and kind of creation, whether material or immaterial, with or without means or precedent, whether first or later.
rows.anchor: her halkı, yaratmanın her türlüsünü bilir; maddeli maddesiz, âletli âletsiz, örnekli örneksiz, gerek ilkin gerek sonra her nev‘ini bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous green trees are merh and afar; rubbing merh against afar like a striker produces fire while their juices are still dripping, a familiar Bedouin practice.
rows.anchor: “merh” ile “afar” denilen iki ağaçtır ki ikisi de yemyeşil suları damlarken

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some imagine one of the two trees as male and the other as female.
rows.anchor: Bunun birini erkek birini dişi menzilesinde de farzetmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proverb says that every tree contains fire, though merh and afar have it abundantly.
rows.anchor: her ağaçta ateş vardır, fakat merh ile afar bol bulmuştur

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some commentators take 'the tree' generically, with merh and afar named as examples.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirler demişlerdir ki ağaçtan murad cinstir. Merh ve afar temsil tarîkiyle zikrolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is not wood or charcoal in a tree, but the heat and ignition that arise through friction and contact from green wood.
rows.anchor: maksud ağaçtaki odun veya kömürü göstermek değil, delk ü temas ile yeşil ağaçtan zuhûra gelen harâret ve işti‘âli anlatmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies this frictional phenomenon as electricity, seeing the verse as a sign of electricity and an example that helps minds approach God's command 'Be.'
rows.anchor: Bu ise şimdi bildiğimize göre bir elektrik hâdisesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire they kindle from it is a certain fact known by practical experiment; experience discloses realities that purely theoretical reason cannot know.
rows.anchor: Demek ki mücerred akl-ı nazarî ile bilinemeyecek hakikatler tecribe ile münkeşif olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator of the heavens and earth can recreate dead people, who are small by comparison, and even recreate the likeness of the whole universe in another existence.
rows.anchor: o çürümüş insanlar gibi küçüğünü hatta bütün o âlemin mislini diğer bir neş’et ile yine yaratmaya kādir değil midir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indeed, God is the abundant Creator and All-Knowing, fully able to create anew.
rows.anchor: ve O öyle Hallâk, öyle Alîm’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills something, His command to it is simply 'Be,' and it comes to be.
rows.anchor: O’nun emri, bir şeyi murad edince ona sâde “ol” demektir, o oluverir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is glorified because sovereignty over everything is in His hand and He disposes of all things as He wills.
rows.anchor: her şeyde dilediği gibi tasarruf eden Sübhân’a

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers may return willingly in faith and gain forgiveness and honor like the Companion of Yasin; those who refuse are eventually dragged back, judged, and punished.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Yâsîn gibi koşa koşa iman ve islâm ile bi’r-rızâ

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he did not know why the reported virtues of Yasin were particular to it until this verse.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri’nden mervîdir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Melekut is an intensive form of mulk, denoting complete sovereignty and the secrets of governing a kingdom.
rows.anchor: “Melekût” yukarılarda da geçtiği üzere “mülk”ün mübalağa sîgasıdır ki tam bir hâkimiyetle saltanatın esrâr-ı idaresi demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following Saffat surah begins as a clarification of God's sovereignty and the return to Him.
rows.anchor: tavzih olmak üzere Ve’s-Sâffati Sûresi başlıyor
